data.raw_text:
This morning had  a real-world lesson in economics and leadership. I was picking up a family friend living for decades in Singapore, and as we pulled into a petrol pump, the conversation took an eye-opening turn about life in India.
He watched the meter and mentioned that back in Singapore—and even in Manila—fuel prices have more than doubled, sent soaring by the war in the Gulf. He was expecting for the same story here.
When the attendant calmly confirmed that the price remained unchanged, the look of surprise on my friend's face said it all. While much of the world is reeling from price shocks, India has managed to hold the line, providing a rare and vital stability for its citizens.
Sometimes, it takes the perspective of a traveler to truly appreciate the quiet, steady hand at the helm that keeps our wheels turning without the burden of global volatility. 

It’s easy to blame leadership when things go wrong, but silent is the praise when things stay right. Maintaining steady petrol prices under global pressure isn't an accident; it’s an achievement. Perhaps the denial of this success comes from the fact that true stability is often invisible to those who benefit from it most.

Thank you @PMOIndia_RC  @narendramodi @PMOIndia @DefenceMinIndia @DrSJaishankar for the work you have done 

As the saying goes: "When you do things right, people won't be sure you've done anything at all."
